questions.question: Insert 50, 30, 70, 20, 40, 60, 80 into an empty BST, in that order. What is the height (edges)?
questions.solutionApproach: 50 is root. 30<50→left. 70>50→right. 20<50,<30→left of 30. 40<50,>30→right of 30. 60<70,>50→left of 70. 80>70,>50→right of 70. Perfectly balanced tree, height=2.

questions.question: Preorder of a BST: 50 30 20 40 70 60 80. Find its postorder WITHOUT drawing the tree, using the partition trick.
questions.solutionApproach: Root=50. Remaining=[30,20,40,70,60,80]. Split by <50/>50: left=[30,20,40], right=[70,60,80]. Recurse left: root=30, remaining=[20,40], split: left=[20],right=[40] → postorder(left subtree)=20,40,30. Recurse right: root=70, remaining=[60,80], split: left=[60],right=[80] → postorder=60,80,70. Combine: (left-post)+(right-post)+(root) = 20 40 30 60 80 70 50.

questions.question: Searching for key 25 in a BST, is the examined sequence [50, 10, 30, 20, 25] a valid possible search path?
questions.solutionApproach: Start range (-∞,∞). 50: within range, 25<50 so narrow to (-∞,50). 10: within (-∞,50), 25>10 so narrow to (10,50). 30: within (10,50), 25<30 so narrow to (10,30). 20: within (10,30), 25>20 so narrow to (20,30). 25: within (20,30), found. All steps consistent — VALID.
questions.answer: Yes, valid — each step consistently narrows the range toward 25.
